column2: I am not as strong as I once was, and the winters bite deeper every year. But who else will tell the young fools of [Root.Capital.GetName] what they are doing wrong? Who else remembers how things were done before them, and chose the rulers they now bow to? The forebears can wait for me a while longer.
I am not going anywhere!

[From.GetTitledFirstName] arrived at my court this morning unannounced, staff in hand and a servant dragging [From.GetHerHis] chests behind. The old [From.GetManWoman] says [From.GetSheHe] is pleased with my rule and wishes to watch it more closely, and to give me [From.GetHerHis] priceless counsel at every meal.
Of course you are welcome! Someone fetch a chair by the fire.
Who do you think you are, old [From.GetManWoman]?

After years of quarrels [From.GetTitledFirstName] has finally left my court in peace. Unfortunately, [From.GetSheHe] now wanders the realm warning every other Elder of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] about how poorly I treated [From.GetHerHim], and how little I listen to the old ones.
I assure you all, [From.GetSheHe] has always been impossible to deal with.
Convince the other §YElders§! to ignore §Y[From.GetFirstName]§!'s complaints about you.
At least there will be some quiet at dinner.

[scoped_ruler.GetTitledFirstName] might be a good and wise ruler, but [scoped_ruler.GetSheHe] has never had an eye for talent among [scoped_ruler.GetHerHis] own kin. A land without a lord is a land without a hearth. Luckily for [scoped_ruler.GetHerHim], I am here to help.
There is but one person fit for this...
Advise §Y[scoped_ruler.GetTitledFirstName]§! to grant one of [scoped_ruler.GetHerHis] §YCounties§! to you.
You need only look at [scoped_recipient_first.GetFirstName]!
Advise §Y[scoped_ruler.GetTitledFirstName]§! to grant one of [scoped_ruler.GetHerHis] §YCounties§! to §Y[scoped_recipient_first.GetFirstName]§!.
[scoped_recipient_second.GetFirstName]'s good name is spotless.
Advise §Y[scoped_ruler.GetTitledFirstName]§! to grant one of [scoped_ruler.GetHerHis] §YCounties§! to §Y[scoped_recipient_second.GetFirstName]§!.
[scoped_recipient_third.GetFirstName] is the most capable [scoped_recipient_third.GetManWoman] I can think of.
Advise §Y[scoped_ruler.GetTitledFirstName]§! to grant one of [scoped_ruler.GetHerHis] §YCounties§! to §Y[scoped_recipient_third.GetFirstName]§!.
Then again, perhaps there is no talent in that house at all.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been pestering me for weeks about how [scoped_potential_count.GetFirstName] would make a model vassal, if only I would give [scoped_potential_count.GetHerHim] a county to prove it.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been pestering me for weeks about how I should share my burdens with [From.GetHerHim] if I want our people to prosper. I cannot shake the feeling that [From.GetSheHe] simply wants more land before [From.GetSheHe] goes to the forebears.
Fine! Whatever you say.
I am the [Root.GetTitle], not you.

It took a long time to convince [From.GetTitledFirstName] of [scoped_potential_count.GetFirstName]'s promise, but I got my way in the end. My [GetFromRelation] will not regret listening to an old [Root.GetManWoman].

It took a long time to convince [From.GetTitledFirstName] that I am still perfectly able to rule more land, and that granting it to me serves the good of [From.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. But I got my way in the end.
The words of a wise [Root.GetManWoman] are hard to dismiss.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has chosen to ignore my words. I cannot believe [From.GetSheHe] would so easily brush aside the counsel of an Elder of [From.GetHerHis] realm, one of those who will choose who rules after [From.GetHerHim]. Such shortsightedness will be remembered.
What a foolish, impertinent child!

It is plain that [scoped_ruler.GetTitledFirstName] is too green and too foolish to bear all the burdens of a [scoped_ruler.GetTitle]. Luckily for [scoped_ruler.GetHerHim], I am here to find someone to share them. Someone who will owe me, not [scoped_ruler.GetHerHim].
Clearly, I must take charge myself.
None can deny [scoped_recipient_first.GetFirstName] has a certain... sparkle.
[scoped_recipient_second.GetFirstName] is such a likeable sort.
[scoped_recipient_third.GetFirstName]'s talents are sure to bloom... eventually.
Then again, perhaps [scoped_ruler.GetSheHe] is better left to [scoped_ruler.GetHerHis] own ruin.

As if [From.GetHerHis] endless prattle were not enough, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been tormenting me for weeks about sharing my burdens as [Root.GetTitle] with one of [From.GetHerHis] spineless favourites, [scoped_potential_count.GetFirstName].

As if [From.GetHerHis] endless prattle were not enough, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been tormenting me for weeks about sharing my burdens as [Root.GetTitle] with [From.GetHerHim], by granting the old [From.GetManWoman] a county of [From.GetHerHis] own.
Whatever will make you stop talking!
It will never happen!
For once it seems I have knocked some sense into [From.GetFirstName]'s thick skull. After a long and lively argument, the [From.GetTitle] has given in to my demands.
Perhaps [From.GetSheHe] is not such a bad [From.GetTitle] after all...

It was too much to hope that [From.GetFirstName] would listen to reason now, after ignoring my counsel for so long. The stubborn [From.GetTitle] has turned me away again and again, too proud and too blind to see the sense in my words.
[From.GetSheHeCap] is a lost cause.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been complaining for some time that nobody listens to [From.GetHerHim] any more, and that the young owe more respect to an Elder of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. In truth, I think [From.GetSheHe] is lonely. The old friends are in their graves, and the fire in [From.GetHerHis] room burns for one.
I will make sure you are not neglected.
I know exactly what you need...
Perhaps a gift will cheer you up.
Wait... [From.GetFirstName] is still alive?

For weeks now [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been telling anyone who will listen that I would make a far better ruler of [scoped_claim_title.GetName] than [scoped_ruler.GetTitledFirstName]. The old [From.GetManWoman] is fed up with [scoped_ruler.GetFirstName]'s lack of respect, and when the Elders next choose, [From.GetSheHe] says, [From.GetSheHe] will remember my name.
That is something to think about...

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has been going about [Root.Capital.GetName] praising [From.GetFirstName], saying [From.GetSheHe] would make a far better [Root.GetTitle] than I do. Perhaps I should not have treated the old one so poorly.
Curse that bitter old fool!

For days now [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been going about [Root.Capital.GetName] praising me as one of the wisest rulers [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] has seen in a lifetime. When one of the oldest of the realm speaks so openly for me, even my enemies must listen.
I have always been fond of [From.GetHerHim].

Having long since judged me worthy, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has decided to spend some of [From.GetHerHis] dwindling days sharing a little of [From.GetHerHis] old wisdom with me, so that I may pass it on to my own heirs.
Tell me of the customs of our forebears.
You must have watched over many rulers in your time...
I would hear the old tales of our people.
Staff of the Elders
A worn walking staff of black wood, notched with the name of every ruler its owners helped to choose. An old Elder hands it on only to one they think worthy.
Rarely, §Y[From.GetFirstName]§! also hands you the §YStaff of the Elders§!.
All the other §YElders§! of §Y[Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]§! will be pleased by your decision.
All the other §YElders§! of §Y[Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]§! will be displeased by your decision.
[Root.GetFirstName]'s duty to [Root.GetHerHis] people has given [Root.GetHerHim] new strength and purpose. The forebears will have to wait.
